exercises.title: First transfer
exercises.statement: Put the value `$2A` in the low byte of register D0, using immediate addressing.
hints: The transfer mnemonic is MOVE, followed by a dot and a size (.B, .W or .L).
A # in front of a value means immediate addressing: the data is inside the instruction itself.

exercises.title: Copying between registers
exercises.statement: Put `$1234` in D1 (word, .W), then copy that word into D2 with a direct register-to-register transfer.
hints: A MOVE.W only changes the 16 low-order bits of the destination register.
The high word of D2 must stay at 0, since it was never initialized.

exercises.title: MOVEQ and sign extension
exercises.statement: Use MOVEQ to put the decimal value **-5** in D3. Look at the 32-bit result: the negative number must be sign-extended across the whole register.
hints: MOVEQ #<value>,Dn loads an immediate byte into Dn, sign-extended to 32 bits.
-5 in two's complement on a byte is $FB.

exercises.title: Writing to and reading from memory (absolute addressing)
exercises.statement: Write the value `$1234` (word) at address `$2000`, then read that value back from memory into D4.
hints: MOVE.W #value,$address writes to memory (absolute addressing as the destination).
MOVE.W $address,Dn then reads that same memory location back.

exercises.title: Indirect addressing through an address register
exercises.statement: Load the address `$3000` into A0 (with LEA), write the value `$ABCD` (word) there through indirect addressing `(A0)`, then read that value back into D5 the same way.
hints: LEA computes an effective address and puts it in an address register, without touching memory.
(A0) means the contents of memory at the address A0 points to, not A0 itself.

exercises.title: Walking through memory with postincrement
exercises.statement: Starting at address `$4000`, write the words `$000A` and then `$0014` one after the other, using indirect addressing with postincrement `(A0)+`. Then, starting again from the beginning of that area, read these two words back (still with `(A0)+`) and put their sum in D6.
hints: MOVE.W value,(A0)+ writes at the address A0 points to, THEN moves A0 forward by 2 (the size of a word).
You need to reload A0 with $4000 using LEA before reading back, since it moved forward during the writes.
